For the second pass. Second pass (west): keep, conf low. t1's size objection does not hold near the silk's bottom edge: the pale patch's face-like part (brow line v ~1653 to chin v ~1700, u 20600-20632) is 45-50 px tall, and the nearest sure face at a similar v, the big-hat man's profile (S2.fig.big_hat_man_south_bank_22045, v 1613-1653 at foot v 1712), is 40 px; a figure standing at the silk's edge is painted larger still. Below the face only the eave's straight hatching (v 1677-1757) and a curved stroke like a hand or sleeve at (20630-20650, 1710-1745) show, so the body would be hidden behind the lower roof band. Which way it looks is not settled: the bumpy west contour (u 20600-20610, bumps at v ~1663-1690) reads as brow, nose and chin looking west (toward the trunk, facing 180), while the dark angled stroke at its east edge (20630-20647, 1657-1677) reads as a profile looking east (facing 0, as recorded). entities.name: smaller boat at the bottom edge, rafted to the second grain boat

A ladder leans from its deck (28575, 1545) up to the second grain boat's after deck (28500, 1420). No cargo or crew read.
entities.vis: part: willow whips cover the bow and most of the deck; the massive willow's head hangs over the stern
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder at the east end (stock u 28815, blade to (28955, 1768)) makes the east end the stern. The setup brief's "man at its east end (28790, v 1590-1680)" is the rudder head and stock with its ropes (t12 agrees; the restyle draws the same mechanism): no figure. The restyle crowds about eight people on and around this boat (u 28450-28870, v 1270-1630): invented. FRONT est: the hull's strakes and its dark lower edge show from u ~28400 east ((28400, 1699) -> (28675, 1724)); west of 28400 only willow whips are drawn, so the bow is at about 28390-28400, hidden. SCALE CUE: front-rear about 415 px; freeboard at u 28575: gunwale v ~1590 -> waterline v ~1715 = 125 px; rudder blade about 160 px long. The ladder (two rails with rungs, about 145 px long) is part of this boat (it may belong to the grain boat: either way river_e's). The rudder blade's tip at u 28955 is 95 px west of the S1 seam.

entities.name: second grain boat (万石船) under the willows
entities.what: A second laden grain boat moored east of the first, bow to bow-stern with it, bow west: a woven-mat hood with a coiled mat on its top over the bow (u 28015-28290, v 1160-1240), a cross beam and posts below it, the dark raked stem descending to the water; the hull and its mat-covered cargo run east under the willow whips; on the after deck (u 28480-28700, v 1280-1430) a pile of heavy coiled cables and a long bundle with two short dark uprights (bitts, or one man and his raised arm: see the low-confidence figure S2.fig.boatman_coils_28543) and a small windlass frame; the stern is hidden behind the massive willow's knobbed head. A ladder runs from its after deck down to the bottom boat (S2.veh.boat_bottom_28395); its mooring line goes to t11's post with a coiled rope at the bank's foot (S2.prop.mooring_post_rope_28272).
entities.vis: part: willow whips cover the hull from u 28150 east; the massive willow's head hides the stern; the bottom boat hides the south waterline
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder is not visible. The dark blade at the west end (28030, 1290) -> (28100, 1470) slopes DOWN and EAST (under the hull), as a raked stem does; a rudder hanging from a west stern would slope down and WEST (aft), as the three visible rudders here slope aft. So bow west (conf med; the restyle also paints a stem there). OTHER READING: the dark blade is a rudder and the west end the stern (t12 reads the east end's coils and windlass as the stern, which agrees with mine): then swap front/rear and facing 10. FRONT = the stem's foot at the water (28095, 1468); the stem head (28030, 1245) overhangs it 70 px west. REAR est at the massive willow's head (the after-deck gear ends about u 28680-28714). Facing 190: we see the bow hood's front face, so the bow turns a little toward the viewer. SCALE CUE: about 600 px front-rear along u (the first grain boat: 600); bow hood 275 px wide; freeboard aft about 50 px (after deck v ~1420 -> water est 1470). The bank porter of t11 (S2.fig.bank_porter_28355) climbs the bank above its mat roof (feet est (28355, 1226) on the bank, not on a plank). The ladder t11 records on the bank slope (S2.prop.ladder_28538, (28492, 1155) -> (28585, 1102)) does not reach this boat on the scan; it is t11's.

entities.name: grain boat (万石船) with the gangplank
entities.what: A big, broad, deep-laden grain boat moored with its rounded bow to the north-west against the bank and its stern toward the viewer: at the bow two overlapping woven-mat roofs (u 27280-27750, v 1000-1110) over a small deckhouse with windows and posts (u 27560-27750); a long spar lying fore-and-aft along the deck (u 27490-27810, v 1128-1147: the lowered mast or a windlass beam); planked hatch covers (u 27305-27500, v 1195-1295) and the cargo under nets of crossing ropes amidships; a high transom stern with an arched gallery roof (u 27760-28010, v 1155-1220), a tiller bar (v 1265-1280) and a big rudder hanging from its centre, the blade reaching (28086, 1593). A cleated gangplank runs from its north gunwale near the stern (27795, 1145) up the bank to (28023, 1050) (nobody on it), and two mooring lines run from the gunwale beside it up to t10's rope coil and stake on the bank top (S2.prop.coiled_rope_27873, S2.prop.mooring_stake_27902). Moored stern to bow with the second grain boat (S2.veh.boat_grain_28095).
entities.vis: part: its north side lies against the bank; the stern's lower part is hidden by the rudder
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder hangs from the east end's transom (stock u 27880-27900 from v 1217 down to the water at ~1500; blade to (28086, 1593)): stern east, toward the viewer; the rounded west end with the mat roofs is the bow. Facing 160: from rear (27882, 1505) to front (27285, 1330) the axis climbs 175 px of v, so the bow points west-north-west into the bank. FRONT est: the bow is round; the outer hull line runs (27268, 1230) -> (27293, 1330) -> (27357, 1400) -> (27464, 1464) -> (27571, 1493) -> (27793, 1514), and the waterline under the stem is taken at (27285, 1330). SCALE CUE: hull 27267-28010 (743 px over all, front-rear 600 px along u); beam seen at the bow from the north gunwale (v ~1120) to the south waterline (v ~1450) at u 27400; freeboard amidships low (deep-laden): south gunwale v ~1440 -> waterline 1493 at u 27570 = 53 px; transom about 250 px wide (u 27760-28010). Gangplank: two rails about 15 px apart with 7-8 cleats, 245 px long. Ropes: two parallel lines from the coil (27885, 982) down the bank to (27865, 1123) and to the gunwale at about (27845, 1150); a frayed end trails east from the coil to (27940, 1003) (t10's). The restyle draws the same boat (blue mats, a windlass) and no crowd on deck.

entities.name: big cabin boat with mat roofs moored by the warehouse
entities.what: A big timber boat moored along the north bank west of the great willow, bow west: a deep planked hull with nail rows; a gable-roofed fore cabin (u 26040-26150) and a long flat-roofed cabin with plank walls and doors behind it to u ~26530, a ladder leaning against the cabin side from the deck to the roof (26255, 840)-(26200, 720), a row of round coiled bundles (rolled mats or rope coils; the restyle draws tied netted baskets) along a woven-mat cover behind the roof (v 650-700), and a long pole lying along the roof (u 26330-26565, v ~645: a spare spar or punting pole); aft, a barrel-vaulted woven-mat hood (u 26490-26700, v 610-720) with three big round bundles, an open arched mat hood over the after deck (u 26700-26800) with a man in its mouth, a raised stern gallery with a lattice rail and an overhanging stern (tip (26845, 707)); under the stern a big rudder on a stock with a drum-shaped head, its lattice blade reaching down and aft into the water. A post with a round head stands on deck at (26365, 725). No mooring line or sweep is drawn. Its bow is hidden behind the stern and rudder of river_m's boat moored just west of it (u 25150-26050).
entities.vis: part: the bow is hidden behind river_m's boat's stern and rudder (u 25850-26100); the great willow's whips cross the stern hood
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the end with the rudder is the stern (rear), the other end the bow (front), per the lead's rule for all river areas. The rudder hangs under the east end (stock at u 26616, head (26600-26645, 870-892), blade u 26600-26790, v 920-1048), and the east end carries the raised stern gallery: stern east, bow west, facing 175 (the hull rises slightly toward the bow). t9 calls the east end the "bow": it is the stern. FRONT is est: the hull's strakes run west behind river_m's boat's rudder (u 25990-26100) with no sign of a stem east of u 26060; a foredeck ahead of the fore cabin (front u 26040) puts the stem at about u 25930-26030. REAR = the waterline under the sternpost where the rudder hangs (the hull's bottom line runs (26075, 970), (26262, 989), (26450, 995), (26606, 1001)); the stern overhangs it by 245 px at deck level. SCALE CUE: hull 25980 (est) to 26845 (overhang) = about 865 px; waterline length front-rear 620 px; freeboard at u 26300: deck edge v 835 (below the cabin walls' foot at 822-831) -> waterline v 990 = 155 px; cabin walls about 95 px (735 -> 830); fore cabin door about 70 px; rudder blade about 190 px long. The hull is drawn deep: this boat rides high (no cargo in the hull). Waterline evidence: the dark bottom strake with current lines below it from v ~1000 and the rudder blade entering the water. Possible mooring: the capped posts t7 reads at u 26018 and 26128 (v 565-630) stand at the warehouse plinth's foot; no rope from this boat reaches them (zoom 3), so they look like the plinth's pillar feet.

DEPTH DIRECTION: the bed's lower edge (25535, 100) -> (25598, 72), slope dv/du -0.44 (it runs mostly east with a little depth; not a good receding edge). front/rear = ground under the crates' outer ends (est). The two lattice crates are not hung level: the west crate (25530-25568, 75-98) stands lower and nearer, the east crate (25570-25600, 33-75) higher and further, one behind the other along a line that runs up to the east as a barrow's bed recedes here. A load on a shoulder pole would hang at one height on either side of its carrier, and the hooded man (25512-25555, v 28-75) is at the west end behind both crates, not between them. No wheel shows: it would be under the crates.

entities.name: boat with a mat canopy and mat cabin, moored before the halls
entities.what: A big plank-built river boat moored along the bank in front of the 沿河雅座 halls, bow west: at the bow a pair of scroll-ended bitt beams (25165-25255, v 660-690) with coiled ropes, its mooring rope running up the bank to t6's post S2.prop.mooring_post_25207; a dark plank hatch cover over the fore hold (25200-25400, v 715-780); a broad dark arched mat canopy on posts over the foredeck (25400-25610, v 528-620) sheltering a lidded jar, a bowl and other gear; a long rounded mat cabin roof (25610-25880, v 595-680) with casks and bundles on and behind it, a domed ribbed basket (25890-25920, v 620-650) and a box (25935-25965, v 625-660) at its east end; a raised hatch board on legs amidships (25605-25760, v 740-780) and curved bamboo hoops (awning frames) along the deck; a high stern with a carved post and a big rudder whose blade hangs to (26105, 1065). Crew: a man leaning on the casks, and faint others under the canopy and at the cabin's east end.
entities.vis: part: its bow's foot hidden behind 逆水行舟's stern blade; its north side behind the canopy and cabin
entities.note: BOW: west (the rudder and the high carved stern at the east end; the lead's rule). WATERLINE: beam_s = the hull's lowest line, v 1005-1010 at u 25500-25800; front est where the stem's line (25140-25160, v 665-880) meets the water behind 逆水行舟's stern blade (u 25000-25285, v 910-1015); rear est under the sternpost, behind the rudder. MOORED TO: S2.prop.mooring_post_25207 (t6) by a rope from the bow bitts, its line (25330, 688) -> (25290, 668) -> (25250, 625) -> (25222, 575) -> the post's coils at (25210, 556) (custom point rope, the far end rope_end). Its west end touches the cargo boat's stern (u ~25150-25170). SCALE CUE: hull about 885 px (25145-26030); hull side from the gunwale (v ~795-840) to the bottom (v ~1008) about 190 px; the crew about 70 px tall at foot v ~600. Freeboard for the frame: gunwale (25600, 800) over waterline (25600, 1008). The restyle paints the river below it (u 25500-26400, v 1000-1790) as dry ground: it is water. The restyle's seated person in red at the cabin's east end is the box (t7). Merge: the "tall figure at its stern" (t8, river_e: u ~26000-26020, v 720-800) reads on the merge crop gen/map/S2/look/merge_stern_26010.jpg as the rudder stock's ribbed, drum-shaped head with its ropes, not a man (no face; vertical ribs); not recorded. The second pass may look again.

entities.name: big two-wheeled cart being loaded
entities.what: Big two-wheeled cart with a long open bed (spoked wheels about the height of a man's chest), standing on the street facing west with its team of two mules hitched in front by long traces. Its load: a large flat bundle covered by a woven mat (a lattice of small cross marks), tilted up at the west end, over a dark hatched heap (straw or sacks). The bed's rails run on past its rear to u ≈ 24518 and a prop stick stands under the rear. A man stands on the bed's front handling the load; a saddled horse (t6's) stands behind its rear.
entities.vis: part: the far wheel hidden; the front half crossed by the team's traces
entities.note: SCALE CUE: near wheel rim u 24355-24427, v 193-267, hub (24390, 227): diameter about 73 px. Bed u 24347-24480, v 160-217; load u 24352-24467, v 118-175 (high at the west end). Front: the shafts or front legs run down from the bed's front (24347, 193) toward (24305-24320, 255-270), where the traces reach the cart (est). Rear: the bed's east end at about 24480; rear prop stick (24460, 210) -> (24470, 240); rails to (24518, 188). DEPTH DIRECTION: the bed's lower edge (24347, 217) -> (24480, 193), dv/du -0.18 (the cart stands nearly along the street, its rear a little north); not a receding edge. The restyle paints the load as straw sheaves.

entities.name: high-sided cargo boat with a hooded bow, moored along the north bank
entities.what: A very long, high-sided boat lying along the north bank, bow west, close beside 逆水行舟 to its south and end to end with 豪华客船 to its west: at the bow (u 23700-23900) a curved arched beam over a dark mat hood, a deck post and a spoked windlass; on deck a flat board platform on legs and big round coils of rope or baskets (23940-24090, v 635-725) and a short ladder leaning from the deck up to the bank (top at (24045, 505)); amidships a flat mat-roofed deckhouse open at the sides (roof u 24275-24583, v 496-530) with a second arched beam and a dark mat hood at its east end (24425-24600, v 586-730); east of it a spoked wheel or windlass on a post (24640-24740, v 523-590); aft a huge rounded mat cover over the cargo, topped with a woven round basket (24775-25137, v 542-667); a high curved stern with a carved post and the rudder stock at u ~25100-25130. A coil or round fender hangs on its south side at (24380, 840), and at the bow a long rope-wrapped fender (or bundle) hangs on a line over its south side, between it and 逆水行舟's foredeck (u 23735-23768, v 745-872). No mast. Its many strakes with rivet rows show it riding high (unladen). Crew: a man at the bow (the spoked windlass beside him is unmanned), one or two men at the aft windlass, two crouching on deck, two in the deckhouse and a man poling at the gunwale.
entities.vis: part: its waterline and lower hull are hidden behind 逆水行舟 all along; its north side behind its own deck
entities.note: ONE HULL OR TWO: one. The rivet rows of its strakes run unbroken from the bow (u ~23710) to the stern (u ~25165) at v ~690-860 (checked at zoom 3 at u 24540-24820, where a second boat's bow would be). THE BRIEF'S "SMALL CANOPIED BOAT" (24250-24500, v 500-600) is read as this boat's midship deckhouse: its two seated men sit at v ~600, on this boat's deck level, and no separate hull, stem or waterline shows under it. Other reading (conf low): a small canopied boat lying in the gap between this boat and the bank, its own hull hidden; it would then need its own entity with the two men as its crew. BOW: west (the rudder stock and the high stern at the east end). WATERLINE: hidden; front and rear est at the feet of the stem and the sternpost where they disappear behind 逆水行舟 (v ~870-880); beam_s est; beam_n est at the deck's north edge (hidden). MOORED: it lies against the bank with its ladder up to it; no mooring rope to a post is visible in u 23700-25150. SCALE CUE: hull about 1430 px (23715-25145); the deck's south gunwale at v ~690-700 and the visible side down to v ~860-880 (about 180 px, much higher than 逆水行舟's 65 px side: riding high, or a higher-sided boat); its crew about 62-67 px tall at foot v ~575-600. Freeboard for the frame: gunwale (24400, 695) over the hidden waterline (24400, ~885 est). The restyle paints knots of 4-5 people at the bow windlass (23750-23980) and at the aft windlass (24600-24740): the scan has 3 and 2-3. Second pass: (1) the 'second figure beside the poler' (retired crewman_beside_poler_23748 (retired at the second pass)) is a long rope-wrapped fender or bundle hung on a line over this boat's south side at the bow: line from a small bar on the planking at (23742-23752, 744-749) down to a scroll-tied top (23731-23766, v 777-797), wrapped body to its tapered foot (23744, 872, est, behind 逆水行舟's bow hood); other reading: a bitt post with scroll ends on 逆水行舟's foredeck. (2) The bow windlass is unmanned on the scan (windlass_man_w_23888 (retired at the second pass) and windlass_man_e_23952 (retired at the second pass) retired as its disc, crank and spoke ends): the crew is 9, not 11. (3) A thin upright stick stands at the deckhouse roof's east end at (24537, 482-500) (t6 left it to river_m): a pole stood upright on the deck, or a stake on the bank behind the roof.

entities.name: 逆水行舟: the big passenger-cargo boat with a mast, towed upstream
entities.what: A long, deep river boat lying in mid-river south of the cargo boat, bow west, being towed upstream: a single mast stepped amidships in a braced tabernacle on the cabin roof at u ~24190, its top at (24183, 302), with a fan of about fifteen stays and lines to both ends of the deck; the tow rope is made fast to the mast at (24188, 375) and runs about 2350 px west over the cargo boat's bow, the bank and the water to the five trackers (t2: S2.grp.boat_towed_mast_23632; the rope's far end is in the lead tracker S2.fig.tracker_lead_21867's hands at (21832, 197)); a short bar is lashed across the rope at (23945, 435-472). A long plank-walled cabin with lattice windows and a door runs the whole length under a low mat roof (cabin walls v ~1030-1140); the bow at the west end has a dark arched mat hood over a low foredeck, a carved stem post and two boat-hooks lying crossed over the stem; the stern at the east end rises over a big rudder whose blade trails at the waterline (24965-25185, v 1160-1220), under a mat awning with a big coil of bamboo rope (24900-25000, v 840-930) and two light boards standing under it, a tall one at u 24732-24789 (v 869-979) and a shorter one just west of the coil at u 24866-24902 (v 920-975); a long dark mat-hatched blade projects east from the stern at deck level to (25285, 1010) (a sweep 橹 shipped aft, or the stern awning's eave). Coiled ropes and bundles on the roof. Crew: a bowman under the hood, a man fending off 豪华客船's stern with a pole, a robed man on the foredeck, three or four men on the roof (one kneeling and hauling a line at the mast), a passenger at a window (perhaps two) and a man at the stern cabin's door. Not moored: it passes the moored cargo boat on its south side, close alongside.
entities.vis: part: its north side is hidden behind its own roof; the bow waterline behind the crossed boat-hooks
entities.note: WHICH HULL CARRIES THE MAST: this (southern) one. The mast is drawn in front of the cargo boat's planking all the way down from v ~460 to its tabernacle on this boat's roof (posts at u ~24185 and ~24222, braces u 24180-24260, v 893-965); a mast stepped in the cargo boat would stop behind that boat's side. The tow rope ends at this mast. BOW: west (the end without the rudder; the lead's rule): the rudder and the projecting blade are at the east end, the hooded foredeck with the bowman at the west, and the trackers haul west. TOW ROPE (custom point rope, a polyline from the mast to the far end, scan px): mast (24188, 375) -> (24100, 400) -> (24016, 430) knot -> (23945, 450) the lashed bar -> (23700, 499) -> its lowest sag v ~518-521 at u 23250-23500 -> (22900, 491) (my reading, matching t3's) -> t3's and t2's readings to the lead tracker's hands at (21832, 197); it runs on through all five trackers' grips (t2). Length along u ~2356 px. FAR END: S2.fig.tracker_lead_21867 (t2), the whole file S2.grp.boat_towed_mast_23632 (t2). WATERLINE: beam_s = the hull's lowest near-side line, v 1200-1215 at u 24300-24900; the bow's waterline est where the stem's lower line meets the hull bottom (23632, ~1100); the stern's est under the sternpost behind the rudder (25050, ~1205); beam_n est (hidden), from the roof's depth (the roof spans v ~820-1000). SCALE CUE: hull 23632-25050 = about 1420 px at the waterline; mast 663 px from its foot to its top; hull side (gunwale wale v ~1140-1150 to bottom v ~1210) about 65 px; cabin wall about 110 px (v 1030-1140); window opening about 95 px tall; the crew on the foredeck about 125-133 px tall at foot v 950-1070. Freeboard for the frame: gunwale (24400, 1145) over waterline (24400, 1212), 67 px; the roof's front edge at v ~1000-1030 over the gunwale; the bow deck (23640, 1068) over its waterline (23640, 1100). Restyle: it adds a second man at the bow (u 23600-23640) where the scan has the carved stem post, and shows the blade at the stern as a blue fish-shaped object. "Rowed by eight men" (sections.md): no oar or sweep is in the water on the scan; the fan of long lines from the mast are stays, and only one man on the roof works a line. Second pass: the light shape under the stern awning at u 24866-24902, v 920-975 is a second, shorter board (retired man_stern_awning_24870 (retired at the second pass)), drawn like the tall one at 24732-24789; a possible second, smaller passenger at the cabin window (S2.fig.second_passenger_window_24050, low); the 'second figure beside the poler' (retired crewman_beside_poler_23748 (retired at the second pass)) is a fender hung from the cargo boat or a bitt post on this foredeck (both readings in the cargo boat's note). Crew 11 -> 10 or 11 with the new low passenger.

entities.name: 豪华客船, the long passenger boat
entities.what: A very long passenger boat moored along the north bank below the terrace, bow west: at the bow a curved post rising from the stem to a netted knob (a lantern cage or fender basket) and a beam with lashings projecting west at deck level; an open fore canopy with a dark mat roof on four posts (u 22465-22560), then a cabin with mat-curtained walls (22580-22700), a long cabin with lattice windows, panelled sills and a door (22700-23300) with a chair or bench back (u 22960-23020, v 720-770) and a table with things on it (u 23090-23140, v 730-770) seen through its openings, an open bay with two passengers (23300-23440), and an after cabin with hanging mat blinds under a dark mat roof (23440-23700) carrying on top a deck with a windlass (23360-23430) and a small arched mat shelter (23490-23640); a narrow side walkway runs outside the cabins. Cargo lies on the roof: coiled ropes, a drum, round baskets and bales, a rolled mat and a big round basket. A ladder leans from the side walkway to the roof at u 23240-23310. A mooring rope runs from S2.prop.mooring_post_23126 to its roof rail. No mast is up; no sweep or rudder shows (the stern is hidden).
entities.vis: part: its stern is hidden behind the bows of 逆水行舟's two hulls (river_m's); the far side is behind the cabins
entities.src: 名画记: 豪华客船 (pin 17); 余辉: 客船启程 (?)
entities.note: ORIENTATION: bow west (conf med): the west end has the raked stem, the curved ornamental post and the projecting beam (S3's river_w reads the same projecting beam at a bow); the east end carries the windlass on the after-cabin roof (a stern windlass hauls the rudder) and a small railed stern panel at (23690-23730, 640-700); the rudder itself is hidden. Other reading: bow east (then swap front/rear, facing 0). The setup's brief calls the windlass deck a "foredeck"; it is the after-cabin roof. 客船启程 (余辉) may be this boat: a man climbs the ladder toward the roof where the mooring rope is made fast, as if casting off; the strokes don't settle it. SCALE CUE: waterline 22545-23725 (about 1180 px); side walkway v ~840 over the waterline v ~910 at u 23200 (70 px); cabin from walkway (v 840) to eave (v ~700) about 140 px; lattice window bays 45-55 px wide; the standing boatman on the walkway is 145 px tall. WATERLINE: the hull's lowest strake: (22545, 775) at the stem, (22700, 850), (22800, 877), (22900, 893), (23000, 903), (23200, 910), (23400, 910), (23560, 900), then hidden; rear est at the stern (u ~23725, behind 逆水行舟's bows) on the level of the amidships waterline. The hull lies at a slant, its bow further north (facing about 172). 逆水行舟's tow rope (river_m's) passes over its roof cargo at v ~490-515.

entities.name: mat-roofed boat moored along the south spit
entities.what: A long boat moored along the low south spit, bow west: a long arched mat roof on posts over its west two thirds (u 22290-22780), with cloths or curtains hanging under its west end; a raked pole (a lowered mast or a stowed quant) leans west from the roof's west post with a cloth (a furled sail?) hanging from it; an open after deck and, at the east end, an overhanging stern frame of lashed beams with a rudder whose stock stands at u ~22885 and whose blade lies along the waterline to u ~23050. A rope runs from its side down to the spit. On the deck under the roof's middle lie a flat woven object (a straw sandal, a folded mat or a basket lid; u 22440-22495, v 1592-1615) and a small staved tub (u 22505-22535, v 1580-1615). A man bends over the near gunwale pouring a bucket into the river.
entities.vis: part: the open boat's east end and the hanging cloth hide its west end
entities.note: ORIENTATION: stern east (the rudder stock and blade and the overhanging stern frame), bow west under the pole; conf med. The pole: from (22190, 1332) to the roof's west post top (22278, 1505), bound at (22215, 1430), a cloth hanging from it to v ~1560; the brief's "pole or mast at ≈ 22100" for the first bottom boat is this pole. Its rope: from the near side at (22555, 1612) to the spit (S2.grd.south_bank_spit_22400) at about (22490, 1672). SCALE CUE: hull 22290-22880 at the waterline (about 590 px), the stern frame to 23062; near gunwale v ~1585 over the waterline v ~1680 at u 22700 (about 95 px); roof posts at u ~22280 and ~22735, roof top v ~1440. The setup's "two cabin boats at the bottom" are the open boat (21965-22240) and this one (22290-23060). Second pass (west): the two small things on the deck under the roof (crop c_deckobj.jpg, i_matboat.jpg; the restyle paints a straw sandal and a wooden tub) were in no entity; as the boat's gear they go in its `what` (the river rule: cargo in `what`).

entities.name: small boat's bow at the silk's edge
entities.what: Only the bow of a small boat shows, coming in from below the silk's bottom edge beside the south bank's flat edge: a pointed dark-hatched bow with a short post and the curve of its near gunwale; the rest of the hull runs off the silk to the south-west. Nobody is seen in it.
entities.vis: part: the silk's bottom edge cuts it below v ~1790
entities.note: Visible hull u 22020-22165, v 1720-1790; front and rear est at the silk's edge (its true length is not painted: builder choice). t2's big man in the broad hat (S2.fig.big_hat_man_south_bank_22045) sits on the bank's edge just west of the bow; read as on the bank (t2), not in this boat. If the merge puts him in the boat, he would be its crew.

entities.name: boat with six men at its great stern sweep
entities.what: A boat in midstream heading west (upstream), its hull running west under the great willow's whips: a planked after deck where six men crowd along the loom of a great sweep (大橹); a stern frame of crossbeams lashed together overhangs the stern eastward to about u 22420, the loom crossing it at a pivot; the sweep's long shaft runs on east-south-east into the water and ends in a broad flat blade with an upturned tip at about u 22945. The stern's side carries a decorated oval panel with two eye-like marks.
entities.vis: part: west of u ~22050 the hull is lost under the great willow's whips (t2's S2.tree.willow_great_21345); its bow is not painted
entities.note: THE "SKIFF" IS THE SWEEP'S BLADE: the long shaft from the men's hands runs unbroken past the stern frame to (22818, 1089), where its two edges spread into a flat blade (u 22780-22945, v 1057-1112) with an upturned tip; there is no gunwale, thwart or second hull line, so it is not a separate boat (S3's river_w boat at 15595 has the same long sweep with five men and a blade in the water). ORIENTATION: stern east (the sweep is worked over it, the lead's rule), bow west (hidden); conf med. Other reading: the eye-marked oval panel could be a bow decoration (then the boat heads east and the sweep is a bow sweep); not taken. The men lean on the loom at about knee height (a bound loom shows at u 22250-22330, v 940-965) where it runs east to the pivot on the stern frame. SCALE CUE: deck edge v ~975-1000; the hull's side drops to the waterline est v ~1080-1115 at u 22100-22200 (the stern rises); the men are 140-157 px tall; sweep about 700 px from the men's hands to the tip. front est at the last hull planks before the whips (u ~22030-22050) less a little; its true bow is unknown (builder choice).

entities.name: open boat tied to the south bank's mound
entities.what: A small open boat with thwarts and floor boards, no cabin, lying at the foot of the south bank's mound; its squared west end is tied by a twisted rope to the mound's face, and small knobs or bollards stand on its far gunwale. A man sits in it, and a second shape crouches at its east end.
entities.vis: part: its east end touches the mat-roofed boat's west end
entities.note: ORIENTATION not painted (conf low): front put at the tied west end; no rudder, sweep or oar shows (the bar under the west end is the hull's near side in perspective). The rope's far end is on the mound's east face (S2.grd.mound_south_bank_21420) at about (21905, 1490); no stake shows. The raked pole with a hanging cloth that rises behind its east end is the mat-roofed boat's (S2.veh.boat_mat_roof_22290). SCALE CUE: about 270 px long; near gunwale v ~1536 over the waterline v ~1559 at u 22100 (a low open boat, about 23 px).

entities.name: small covered boat off the south bank (bow east)
entities.what: A small boat lying off the south bank under the great willow's whips, with a mat canopy on four thin posts over most of its length (u 20880-21240, v 1060-1110; gabled at its east end) and a squared, raised bow board at the east end (u 21190-21215, v 1145-1200); a man sits under the canopy beside a small upright figure or tall vase, and a round basket lies on the deck at the west (u 20985-21010, v 1185-1205). No mast, oars or sweep are painted; people on the bank in front of it (t1's group) reach or hold something up toward it.
entities.vis: part: willow whips cross the whole boat; its west end and its near waterline are hidden
entities.note: WHICH END IS THE BOW (conf low): the east end shows a squared, raised bow board and no rudder; the west end tapers under the willow whips (u ~20870-20900, v 1220-1240) and is hidden. Read bow east (facing ~1); other reading bow west (front (20875, 1242), facing ~181). WATERLINE est: gunwale (21200, 1165) -> (21000, 1215) -> (20880, 1225); the hull's lower edge reads at v ~1210-1240 through the whips (t1: v ~1210-1235), so the waterline is est at v ~1235-1242. SCALE CUE: length ~335 px; canopy ~55 px above the gunwale at the posts (posts at u ~21095 and ~21200); the seated man ~70 px from head to deck. Restyle: it draws the mat canopy as a tiled pavilion roof (an invention) and the upright shape beside the man as a child. Possibly 余辉's 船侧祭神 (an offering at a boat's side): the bank man (t1's S2.fig.bank_man_seated_21140) holds up a small round object toward it, and the boat carries a tall vase-like thing; unconfirmed, not tagged.

entities.name: big cabin boat moored along the north bank (bow west, rudder east)
entities.what: A big river boat moored along the north bank in front of the shops, bow to the west-north-west: a curved stem head with a round windlass hub at the bow (u 21110-21190, v 155-210) and a long oar or pole slanting down from the bow into the water (to about (21265, 318)); a flat mat awning on posts (u 21220-21350, v 160-200) over a row of six coiled ropes hanging along the far gunwale (u 21225-21350, v 195-225); a short upright post on deck (u ~21362, v 150-200); a low cabin with a window (u 21290-21400, v 240-300) where a man sits; a big round-arched cabin frame (u 21400-21500, v 200-300) and a deckhouse with a sloping mat roof (u 21430-21660, v 160-280); a high stern with a gabled rudder house (u 21650-21800, v 170-260) and a big rudder hung over the stern, its blade in the water (u 21650-21780, v 345-420). The hull is planked with rows of nails and bellies down to v ~388 under the deckhouse. No mast or sail. Three crew are painted.
entities.vis: part: willow whips of the south willow's crown cross the hull's lower half west of u 21550; the bow's waterline is hidden
entities.note: WHICH END IS THE BOW (conf high): the rudder hangs over the east end (stock from (21672, 280), blade (21650-21780, 345-420) in the water) under a gabled rudder house: the east end is the stern, by the lead's rule; the west end carries the curved stem head and a windlass hub. WATERLINE: the hull's lowest near-side planks, (21400, ~345) -> (21540, 388) -> the stern (21665, 387); toward the bow it is hidden behind willow whips and est along the same line (slope ~0.2) to (21120, 300). The diagonal from (21110, 230) to (21265, 318), with a dark blade-like wedge at u 21200-21260, v 290-320, is read as a long oar or pole from the bow into the water (part of the boat); it could also be the bow's forefoot. HEADING: rear -> front rises ~87 px of v over 545 px of u: about 12 deg north of west (facing ~168) at dx ~40 px/m. SCALE CUE: waterline length ~545 px (21120-21665); stem head v ~170 over the bow's est waterline ~300 (130 px); the stern's top v ~255 over its waterline 387; crew painted ~80-85 px tall (est feet). The upright post (21362, 150-200) is part of the boat (a bitt or short pole on deck); t2 recorded it as a bank mooring post (S2.prop.post_north_bank_21364, conf low): keep one at the merge. entities.name: second bare tree on the south bank, behind the hall's west roof (uncertain)
entities.what: A bare tree (a small pollard, or a bare deciduous tree) on the south bank east of the great dark-trunked tree: a fan of long, thin, straight bare stems rising from a point just above the south-bank hall's west hip and spreading up and east over the water among the dark tree's shoots.
entities.vis: part: its foot hidden behind S2.bld.south_bank_hall_21050's roof; its twigs mix with S2.tree.dark_trunk_willow_20530's shoots
entities.note: Added at the merge: S3's t9 saw "a second bare tree whose twigs fan over 20650-20950, v 930-1390, its trunk hidden behind that roof (~20680, 1330 est)" (seen east of the seam, for S2) and its twigs mixing with the dark tree's east of 20650; river_w read "uprights at u 20610-20690" as forked branches of the dark tree; t1 recorded one tree, whose shoots it gives out to crown_e (20830, 800). Merge crops gen/map/S2/look/merge_tree_20705.jpg (zoom 1.4) and merge_tree_20705_foot.jpg (zoom 3): a separate set of stems converges downward at u ~20650-20715, v 1300-1455, 60-100 px east of the dark tree's knobbed head (u 20515-20610, v 1230-1380), to a narrow foot just above the hall roof's hip line (v ~1470 here); base est there (the true foot is behind the roof, on the bank between the water, bank top v ~1265, and the hall). READINGS: its own tree (taken, conf low), or the east shoots of S2.tree.dark_trunk_willow_20530 (t1, river_w); then retire this one. For the second pass: the tree count matters to the user. Second pass (west): keep as its own tree (conf low). On a greyscale contrast-stretched crop (g_fan.jpg, zoom 1.35, u 20430-20960, v 880-1500) and at zoom 2.2-3 (g_tree20705.jpg, z_frame20720.jpg), the stems split into two sets: (1) the long straight shoot at u ~20645 (v ~900-1340) and its neighbours bend west into the dark tree's knobbed head at v ~1340-1370 (its east edge u ~20615): they are S2.tree.dark_trunk_willow_20530's; (2) two or three stems at u 20700-20720 run down past the head's level, about 90 px east of its edge, converging to the hall roof's west hip line at about (20710, 1455-1480), where they stop as if behind the roof, and fan up and east toward u 20850-20950, v 950-1100. A drooping willow whip would spread downward, not converge, so set (2) reads as a separate stem whose foot is hidden behind the roof, as S3's t9 saw. Between the two sets, at (20720-20760, 1330-1400), a pale shape with folds that the restyle paints as a wooden frame with a wheel and a hanging cloth reads on the scan as a gap between the stems and the hip (no frame strokes). Points kept; its crown_w (20640, 940) may lie on the dark tree's shoot: the lead may move it to about (20690, 1000). FRAME AGENT (second pass accepted): crown_w moved from (20640, 940) to (20690, 1000), as the second pass offered: the long shoot at u ~20645 is S2.tree.dark_trunk_willow_20530's, so this tree's crown starts at its own stems' west edge.

Trunk: u 20412-20610 at v 1350-1560 (a dark mass on its west side at u 20412-20460, v 1350-1500 is shadow or a second stem), u 20465-20600 at v 1600-1776; knobbed head u 20515-20610, v 1230-1380; pale limb from (20487, 1350) up to (20394, 1094); shoots' tips about v 700-760 over u 20310-20600, and out to u ~20830 at v 750-1000 (east tips mix with the whips of t2's great willow). A pale patch between its east side and the south-bank roof's west eave (u 20600-20645, v 1630-1700) reads at a glance like a profile face, but at 45 x 60 px it is twice a figure's head here: the gap between trunk and eave brackets (the restyle draws a wall and brackets). entities.name: 王家纸马铺: the Wang family's paper-offerings shop

entities.name: plain-walled house with the pole scaffold on its roof
entities.what: A single-storey tiled house on the bank with a long plain plastered front wall (no door or window painted) under a valance of scalloped hanging cloth and a bracket frieze; its roof has a light triangular gable facing the river in its east half, with a lattice board under the gable, and a small hip-gable end at its west end. A great scaffold of lashed poles stands on the roof ridge running back from the gable: uprights, two or three levels of cross-bars and braces, the pole tips sharpened and splayed like a crown (u 24880-25240, up to the silk's top edge). A long pole sticks out west from the scaffold's foot with a banner of three dark vertical stripes on light cloth with a wavy hem hanging from it. At the west end a big curved mat awning sweeps out and up from the wall over a stall (the stall, its table and people are t6's), held by a post at the wall's west corner. No writing on the house itself. A two-lobed ridge-end ornament (鸱尾) stands on the main ridge's west end (u 24829-24849, v 247-269).

Second reading: a free-standing building scaffold on the ground behind the house, its feet hidden by the roofs. The restyle draws it the same; the restyle's willow at u 24600-24900 is the scaffold's pole tips plus t6's pole stack and this banner. Second pass (middle) and FRAME AGENT: the west knob at the ridge's west end is the ridge-end ornament (the two lobes join a neck that runs straight into the ridge line at ridge_end_w; g_ridge.jpg, zoom 6), so t6's head_over_roof_w_24840 (retired at the second pass) is retired; the east knob stays a low head (S2.fig.head_over_roof_e_24867), or a ridge beast.

If the lead takes reading (b), the footprint folds into S2.bld.long_house_22780 and this entity is retired.

entities.name: the wharf road along the north bank of the 汴河 (S2's route)
entities.what: The walk along the canal's north bank from the Rainbow Bridge's north foot to the 望楼饭铺 sheds: a narrow strip between the shop fronts and the moored boats in the west, the trackers' open bank, the strip in front of the gateway and the long house, through the riverside dining terrace, past the open-air eatery and across the wide unloading yard, then along the narrow bank in front of the scaffolded building and the long halls, past the great willow and the jetty, through the grain porters' wharf and along the long shed's front to the countryside.
entities.vis: part: hidden behind the moored boats at u 20900-21700 and 25450-26600, and through the terrace (u 22920-23500)
entities.note: DATUM AND SEAMS: point 0 is S3's route point at exactly u 20500, (20500,258) est, copied from gen/map/S3/parts/structures_w.json with its edges (edge_n 215, edge_s 280). The last point is exactly u 29050: (29050,730), S1's datum: the open ground in front of the 望楼饭铺 shed's east end, just south of the rider's animal (hooves v ~690, t12); bare open ground runs on east at v ~650-860 in front of S1's stalls. EDGES: edge_n is where the open ground stops at building fronts, walls, fences, stalls and tables; edge_s is the river agents' bank_top (the level ground's edge nearest the water: river_w 20500-21850, river_m 23300-26000, river_e 26000-28900), copied at my stations; between 21850 and 23300 river_w2's part had not landed, so edge_s there is my est (t3: shore v ~470-500). No road edge is drawn anywhere. WEST (20500-21750): a strip only 25-65 px of v deep between the shop fronts and fences (v 100-141) and the moored boats (bank_top behind them, v 162-232). TRACKERS' BANK (21750-22300): the centre follows the trackers' towpath diagonal (their feet run (21867,235)->(22172,386)) and passes south of the split willow's feet ((22225,290), (22345,318), t3); river_w puts the bank_top at (21850,248) and the trackers on the top of the wash slope: river_w2's bank line decides edge_s here. HOUSES (22300-22920): between the screen/wall/gate/long house fronts (v 302-414) and the bank. TERRACE (22920-23500): no open ground: the dining terrace fills the bank (its front floor on posts over the slope, stilts to v 485-495). TWO READINGS: (a, taken) through the terrace's floor, from its west end by the long house's east doors and the head of the stone steps to its open east side by the pavilion, est v ~422-425, like S3's route through the tavern's open front (the lead's note for S3); the floor is about ground level at its back and on posts at its front, so the frame may give this range `terrace floor: S2.bld.river_terrace_23250` (a support_ranges entry) or ground; (b) behind the terrace, between it and the hall behind (hidden; the two roofs leave no room on the silk). The builder records the choice. EATERY AND YARD (23500-24600): in front of the panelled screen and the shelter's front posts (v 395-417), then across the wide unloading yard (open ground v ~180-490 between the top shops' tables, the cart and the bank), where the porters walk. WHERE THE HALLS FILL THE BANK (24600-26600): THE ROUTE TAKES THE NARROW BANK IN FRONT OF THEM, not the far street at the top. Evidence: (1) it is continuous with the unloading yard (the porters walk from the yard toward the boats at u 24425-24563, v 400-470, and the strip in front of the scaffolded building's wall foot (v ~500) opens from it, south of the stall under the building's sweeping west eave); (2) people stand on it (t7's two men, feet (25333,568) and (25367,587)) and a mooring post stands on it (t6's at (25207,548)) and the warehouse plinth's capped posts face it (u ~26018 and 26128); (3) at its east end it runs past the great willow onto the wide east bank where the jetty, the sheds' fronts, the sack porters and the 望楼饭铺 shed's customers are, and on to S1's stalls at v ~650-750, the datum S1 needs; (4) the far street (v 15-150, u ~24700-26900) is cut by the silk's top edge, shows only between and behind the halls' roofs, and runs into the top street at 王家纸马铺 and the 望火楼, which does not reach the ground at u 29050 (roofs and willow crowns there). WIDTH (a real-size problem for the frame and the builder): the level strip is only v ~500-520 in front of the scaffolded building (24700-25230; river_m: wash slope v 520-600 below it, where the mooring post stands), v ~555-613 in front of the halls (posts' feet v ~555), v ~600-641 in front of the warehouse and its plain wall: 10-60 px of v, 0.2-1.2 m at 51.25 px/m, plus the wash slope. At u 25450-26600 it is hidden behind the moored boats' mat roofs (est). It stays inside the painted area. The far street is a side street (structures_e). EAST BANK (26600-29050): north of the great willow's foot (t8/t9: (27068-27072, 893-905), on the slope), along the jetty's deck and the lower shed's front (river_e: the jetty's deck edge is the bank_top, at street level, u 27100-27400), across the porters' wharf just north of the sack piles (sacks v ~813-920) and along the long shed's front (posts' feet v ~640-690). Edges east of 24600 are my reading for structures_e to check. All edge and centre points hidden behind boats, buildings or willows are est. MERGE (2026-10-12): edge_s at the stations u 21950, 22100, 22285 and 22450 now lies on river_w2's bank_top (S2.grd.north_bank_22550: 311 est, 380, 441, 430), replacing this agent's estimates (300, 400, 440, 450), as its note asked. From u 22600 to 23300 river_w2's bank_top (418, 418, 407, 420, 432) runs north of this road's centre (410, 445, 448, 422, 425): the level strip in front of the long house is 5-15 px deep in river_w2's reading and the centre here runs on the wash slope, so those edges are unchanged and the frame step or the lead settles it. The steps at the terrace's west end are S2.str.landing_steps_22950 (river_w2's; structures_w's copy retired). FRAME: support_ranges u 22920-23500 on `terrace floor: S2.bld.river_terrace_23250` (structures_w's reading (a): the route runs through the terrace's floor); the frame gives that floor H 0 (its sill v 438-456 is level with the bank top), so the heights do not change; the range records the reading for the builder. Not changed: u 26100 (the warehouse plinth's foot, v 625-632, is the bank top itself, south of the centre's est v 615: the route runs on the plinth's front or the strip is nil; a question in the frame).

entities.name: the 汴河 at the grain wharf (汴水悍激)
entities.what: The 汴河 along the east wharves: open water left as plain silk and drawn all over with long, flowing, roughly horizontal current lines, curling crests and eddy spirals (汴水悍激, "the Bian's fierce current"); boats moored along its north bank: the mat-cabin boat west of the great willow, the two grain boats (万石船) and a smaller boat south of the second one. No south bank is painted: the silk's bottom edge cuts the water. At the east end the water runs out under the massive willow at the bottom right.
entities.vis: part: the moored boats hide the north shore from u 26000 to 26790 and from 27245 to 28720; willow whips and the massive willow's head hide it east of 28400
entities.note: No shore is inked. shore_n is read where the bank's ink-wash smudges end and the thin wavy current lines begin. West of the great willow it is hidden behind the mat-cabin boat (the bank in front of the warehouse shows only to v 640-650, where the boat's roof begins; est v 655-680; the true line could lie anywhere down to about v 850 behind the hull). East of the boat's stern the first current lines show at (26815, 890); the shore then runs down the wash-drawn bank below the willow and the jetty to v 1040-1110 (u 26960-27150; a dark wash tongue reaches v ~1150 at u 27100-27225). OTHER READING at the willow: t8/t9 put the willow's roots (27068, 905) at the water's edge, which would lift the shore there by about 150 px; I read the smudges at v 930-1100 below the roots as bank wash, not water (conf low). Behind the grain boats it is est at the boats' north gunwales (v 1110-1160); at u 28297-28357 it is t11's edge line under the bank porter (v 1203-1234); east of 28400 under willow whips and the massive willow's knobbed head (est). EAST END: the line turns south along the massive willow's west foot and meets the silk's bottom edge at about (28968, 1780, est), just east of the bottom boat's rudder tip (28955, 1768) and west of the willow's roots (u 28942-29255, v 1725-1787): no water is painted east of the willow (bare silk with bank wash at u 29150-29400, v 1450-1780), so the water does not reach the S1 seam at 29050. WEST END: (26000, 665, est), hidden behind the mat-cabin boat; river_m's line continues west. No shore_s: the silk's bottom edge (v ~1780 at u 26200-28700, measured) cuts the water all along the reach. 汴水悍激 (pin 7, u 26670): the current lines fill u 26000-27270 from v ~1000 (below the mat-cabin boat; from v ~890 east of its stern) to the silk's edge, densest and longest at v 1050-1500; eddy spirals at (26300, 1185) (a large one, rings over u 26120-26415, v 1155-1210), (26680, 1222), (27022, 1223) and (26908, 1495); thinner lines continue under and between the grain boats (u 27270-28100, v 1500-1780). The restyle's east half paints u 25500-26400 v 1000-1790 as dry grassy ground (its first draw, kept): it is water on the scan.

Three big boats fill its northern half: 逆水行舟 under tow, the high-sided cargo boat beside it and the boat moored before the halls; south of v ~1230 the water is open and empty to the silk's edge.

Ripple motifs (short paired curls) are drawn all over the open water, densest at v 1250-1650; nothing in this reach is drawn as a strong current (汴水悍激, pin 7, is further east, river_e). No strong current lines here (汴水悍激 is further east).

SEAM POINTS: u 21850 shore_n (21850, 425, est), shore_s (21850, 1418, est: behind the mound's crest); u 23300 shore_n (23300, 500, est); shore_s ends at the silk's edge (22680, 1790). Water: open silk with ripples at u 22300-23450, v 920-1480 (nothing floats there). entities.name: the 汴河, west reach of the canal (u 20500-21850)

entities.name: north bank of the 汴河 at the east wharves

entities.vis: part: the boats, the jetty, the great willow's trunk and the willow whips cover much of it
entities.note: bank_top is where the level ground ends: the warehouse plinth's foot (v 628-632 at u 26000-26230; t7 reads the bank strip at v 555-640) and the plain wall's front (v ~640 at 26450); under the great willow's knob head (est, its lower edge at (26890, 676)); from u 27100 to 27400 the jetty's deck edge (the jetty stands at the top of the slope, its posts' feet on the slope); the lower shed's front and t10's mooring stake on the bank top (27902, 985); t11 reads the top at v 970-985 over u 28100-28400; est under the willows further east. The slope between bank_top and shore is narrow in the west (hidden behind the boat) and 250-300 px of v deep at u 26900-28400 (a long gentle slope, not a face). Bank top taken at street level (H 0). Things on the bank are the tiles' (t8-t12) and structures_e's; the wattle fence under the knob head (26850-26970, v 625-662) is left to structures_e. FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like the river's shores; its bank_top on the ground.

entities.name: north bank of the river, u 23300-26000

Nowhere a vertical face, stair or quay in this reach; the boats lie with their north sides against the slope.
entities.vis: part: the bank's foot is hidden by the boats everywhere

FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like the river's shores; its bank_top on the ground.

entities.name: low spit at the bottom edge
entities.what: A low spit of dark-washed ground with clumps of low growth at the bottom of the silk, under the mat-roofed boat moored along it; it runs off the silk's bottom edge at u ~22680.
entities.vis: part: the mat-roofed boat's hull and its bucket man's pour overlap its top edge

entities.name: north bank from the trackers to the terrace

entities.name: south bank's flat edge by the open boat
entities.what: The flat, light top of the south bank between the thatched roof and the water, ending in a straight low edge where the big man in the broad hat sits (t2's), with the water in front of it south of the open boat.
entities.vis: part: t2's big seated man and timber frame stand on it; the small boat's bow cuts its east end
entities.note: Edge points (21550,1637), (21890,1673), (22127,1733) as t2 read them, checked here; ripples run down to the edge at u 22050-22130 (south of the open boat), so the edge is the shore there. FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like the river's shores; its bank_top on the ground.

entities.name: south-bank mound: a long low earth bank at the water
entities.what: A long, low, rounded earth bank on the south side of the river east of the great willow, drawn in grey ink wash with a dark band of low growth along its crest and a small shrub at its west end; water lies north of it, and the thatched and tiled roofs of the south bank run along its southern foot. Its east end slopes down to the water by the open boat at u ~21980.
entities.vis: part: its north foot is hidden right behind the crest's silhouette; its south foot under the roofs
entities.note: bank_top = the crest's silhouette against the water (zoom 1.5-2 on the scan; t2's reading of the crest agrees within 5 px: (21600, 1402), (21700, 1402), (21800, 1403), (21870, 1440)). The shore is taken at the crest: the water shows right above it. The body of the mound is the wash at v 1430-1530 between the crest and the roofs (the roof's ridge from (21380, 1450) to (21900, 1650) is structures_w's). The dark band of low growth along the crest (u 21630-21810, v 1398-1420) is part of this mound; the shrub at its west end is t2's S2.tree.shrub_mound_21605. East of 21850 (river_w2's look range) the crest falls to the water at about (21960, 1530) beside the open boat. t2 left the mound to structures_w; recorded here as the south bank's own ground feature (the banks are the river agents'). If structures_w also records it, keep one. Height: crest about 30-40 px above where its foot would be, i.e. a low bank (est 0.5-1 m). Merge: river_w2 recorded the same mound as S2.grd.south_bank_mound_21700 (retired as a duplicate); its crest (21413, 1407), (21480, 1430), (21547, 1428), (21600, 1402), (21700, 1402), (21800, 1403), (21840, 1420), (21870, 1440), (21910, 1480), (21960, 1530), (21980, 1545) agrees with this one within 5 px and runs 20 px further east to (21980, 1545), where river_w2's S2.grd.south_bank_flat_21850 begins; the open boat's rope ends on its east face at (21905, 1490). structures_w's crest reading also agrees (it recorded none). FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like the river's shores; its bank_top on the ground.

entities.name: north bank of the canal, u 20500-21850
entities.what: The north bank: a narrow earth strip in front of the shops and wattle fences along the silk's top edge, with two pollarded willows at its west end; the boats are moored along it the whole way, so its edge shows only east of the big cabin boat's stern (u ~21720-21850), where it falls to the water in a wash-drawn slope under the trackers' path.

The strip is very narrow: about 30-60 px of v between the shop fronts and the water (under 1-1.5 m at the frame's depth rate). Merge: seam points set: shore (20500, 310) est (S3's); at u 21850 bank_top (21850, 274) est, the mean of this unit's 248 and river_w2's 300 (on the merge crop the level ground under the lead tracker ends at v ~270-280 where the dark bank tufts begin), shore (21850, 345) est. entities.name: south bank of the canal, u 20500-21420 (west of the mound)
entities.what: The near (south) bank at the west end: low ground under the big tiled roofs at the silk's bottom, crossed at its west end by the branches of the dark-trunked tree, the people standing and sitting at the water's edge opposite the small covered boat, and the great knobbed willow at its east end, whose crown hangs over the river.

entities.name: the open-air eatery under its shelter (west of the shop fronts)
entities.what: The open-air eatery on the north bank between the terrace's pavilion and the shop fronts: tables and benches under and in front of a mat shelter on posts, nearly all empty; one man sits at its west end and one stands at the shelter's east post.
entities.note: Merge: t4's S2.grp.eatery_west_23650 (west of u 23700) and t5's S2.grp.eatery_east_23820 (east of it) were folded into this group, as both asked; the shelter S2.bld.eatery_shelter_23750 (structures_w) joins it. t4's list of t5's furniture matches t5's props (t5's seam notes); t4's "stake on the tow rope" at (23940, 455) is the rope's toggle (river_m: rope_toggle), not an entity.

entities.name: the mat-cabin boat and its crew
entities.what: The big mat-roofed cabin boat moored by the warehouse, with a boatman crouching on its cabin roof and a man in its stern hood.

entities.name: the west grain boat and its crew
entities.what: The west grain boat (万石船) moored at the bank with its gangplank down to the shore, a man (?) at its rudder head; its grain is what the porters (t10's and t11's groups) carry ashore to the sack piles.

entities.name: the second grain boat and its crew
entities.what: The second grain boat under the willows with one man (low confidence; or a bitt) among the coiled cables on its after deck.

entities.name: 逆水行舟: the towed boat, its crew and its five trackers

entities.name: the moored boat's crew

entities.name: 豪华客船 and the people on it

entities.name: the open boat and the two in it

entities.name: the mat-roofed boat and its bucket man

entities.name: people on the south bank by the small covered boat

entities.note: The brief placed 'the people by the shed' at u ~20900-21100; they are at u 21047-21282, v 1230-1445. Two members are conf low (see their notes).

entities.note: t10 holds this group (brief). Members owned by t11 (by what and where, for the merge to add): the man with his back to the viewer handing something to the next man (foot about (28162, 791), head (28153, 658)); the man in a hat receiving from him (head about (28220, 646)); the man holding a tally stick upright (u about 28245-28290, v 610-785); the young man bending over the heap with a dark pouch or tally (head (28211, 773), feet hidden at about (28215, 900)); the porter with a sack on his shoulder (u about 28230-28300, v 805-960); the porter with a big sack on his back walking east (u about 28300-28380, v 800-940); the porter carrying a sack up the bank (about 28230-28390, v 1100-1230); sacks at u 28200-28240 (v 893-933). river_e's: the grain boat with the gangplank (its plank lands at about (28023, 1050)) and anyone on the plank (nobody is on it on the scan between u 27800 and 28030). The three men handing over tallies or clasping hands (t10's "tally men": S2.fig.handshake_youth_28163, S2.fig.bowing_man_28270, S2.fig.staff_man_28266) keep their own group S2.grp.handshake_28220, a vignette inside this scene.

entities.name: seller at his tub

entities.name: man raising the pennant frame
entities.what: A man at the lower shed's east end holding up the lower end of one of the two leaning poles that carry a cord of small pennants.

entities.name: the grain boat's mooring on the bank

entities.name: the diner at the table in the shed's east end

entities.name: two people talking on the north-bank strip
entities.what: On the narrow strip of bank in front of the shops, a man in a long robe stands with a smaller figure beside him, as if talking.

entities.name: the open shop at the top of the silk
entities.what: Inside the open front of a shop at the top of the silk, a figure sits behind a table or counter and another stands at the east bay (both faint).

entities.name: the timber and the crouching man

entities.name: the shop fronts east of the eatery
entities.what: Two open shop fronts east of the eatery serving food or tea: inside, a black-capped man and a man in a head-cloth sit talking across a small table, and a topknot man sits in the next doorway; two tables with long benches are set out on the street in front, empty.
entities.note: The shop buildings (lattice screens, doors, a round object hung on the wall at about (24063, 120)) are structures_w's.

entities.name: the cart being loaded on the bank street
entities.what: A big two-wheeled cart stands on the street facing west, hitched by long traces to a team of two dark mules; a man on its bed handles the mat-covered load, the carter leans over the lead mule, and a capped helper stands behind the cart's rear.
entities.note: t6's S2.ani.horse_24565 (a saddled horse standing behind the cart's rear, facing it) and S2.fig.man_at_horse_head_24506 (the man at its head) belong with this scene: the merge should add them. The figure in the shop door behind the cart (S2.fig.man_in_shop_door_24415) may be a helper too.

entities.name: porters carrying sacks along the bank
entities.what: Porters in short jackets, each bent under a big sack on his back, walking west in a file along the bank between the cart and the moored boats.
entities.note: A third porter of the same file is t6's S2.fig.sack_porter_24537 (feet about (24533, 465)); the merge should add him. A fourth sack-carrier bent under a sack shows above the small canopied boat's roof at about u 24440-24500, v 450-500 (feet hidden; on the boat or stepping onto it): river_m's. Merge: t6's S2.fig.sack_porter_24537 and river_m's S2.fig.sack_porter_bank_edge_24467 (the man bent under a sack at the bank's edge above the cargo boat's deckhouse, merge crop gen/map/S2/look/merge_bankedge_24450.jpg: a third figure, distinct from S2.fig.sack_porter_24452 whose feet are at v 432) joined the file.

entities.name: the stall under the scaffolded building's west eave
entities.what: A small stall set out under the sweeping west eave of the scaffolded building on the bank: a table heaped with goods, a dark-clad figure at its west end and a head behind it.
entities.note: The eave and the building are structures_e's. Heavily ambiguous at the scan's resolution: see the members' notes.

entities.name: two men talking on the bank
entities.what: Two men stand face to face on the bare bank between the open shop and the moored boat's stern, talking: one in a light open robe facing out, one with a stick seen from behind.
entities.note: The boat moored just south-east of them (stern at u ≈ 25400-25450, v 540-700) is river_m's.

entities.name: guests in the hall's west window
entities.what: In the west window of the long riverside hall (沿河雅座) a man in a dark robe sits by a low table with a smaller figure beside him.

entities.name: the crate barrow on the far street
entities.what: Two men move a small barrow loaded with two lattice crates east along the far street above the halls: one bent over its west end pushing, one at the shafts' east end pulling.
entities.note: conf low as a whole: see the pusher's note for the shoulder-pole reading.

entities.name: the awning stall on the far street
entities.what: A small stall under a propped cloth awning on the far street above the halls: a table, with a man standing at it.

entities.name: the round-topped cart and its horse
entities.what: A round-topped cart stands parked on the far street with a dark horse or mule feeding, head down, at its east end.
entities.note: The donkey facing them from the east (S2.ani.donkey_26098) may belong too. FRAME AGENT (second pass accepted): the cart's front moved to where its bed ends (25998, 136, est); close posts stand between the bed and the horse and no shaft reaches it, so the horse stands at the cart's east end, not in its shafts. Kept in this group as one parked scene.

entities.name: the stall under the shed on the far street
entities.what: A food or goods stall under an open shed on the far street: the keeper behind the table with its goods, and perhaps a second person at its east end.
entities.note: The shed's roof and posts are left to structures_e.

entities.name: two men at a table on the far street
entities.what: Two men at a small table on the far street, one in light clothing at its west end beside a large wheel, one in a dark robe at its east end, facing each other across it.
entities.note: The wheel S2.prop.wheel_26343 stands just west of the light-clad man.

entities.name: hooded rider at the paper shop
entities.what: A hooded rider on a donkey stopped on the far street facing 王家纸马铺's signboard.
entities.note: The shop's building is structures_e's (S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100 in the brief).

entities.name: the eatery under the mat awning and the parasol (喝杯小酒)
entities.what: The west eatery shed's furniture: three empty tables (one with a bench) in a diagonal row under the mat awning, a fourth under a big round parasol, and a tub at the east shed's post, with possibly one keeper standing behind the tub. No customers are painted at these tables.
entities.note: The shed's posts, mat awning, tiled roof, floor and the railing along its south edge (the jetty) are structures_e's and river_e's. The east shed's tables and its standing figures (u 27590-27750, v 670-840) are t10's; they may belong to the same eatery.
